# ☘️ March: St. Patrick's Day

> Shamrocks, gold coins and a pint at the end of the rainbow

March is St. Patrick's Day: dark, shamrock and lime greens with a pot of gold.

Shamrocks, top hats, rainbows and a pint of beer, with the first hint of spring.

<p><img src="vscode-preview-dark.svg" width="49%" alt="March in VS Code, dark"> <img src="vscode-preview-light.svg" width="49%" alt="March in VS Code, light"></p>

- **Holidays:** St. Patrick's Day (Mar 17); Spring equinox (Mar 20, around the 20th)
- **Mood:** lucky, festive, fresh, cheerful
- **Modes:** dark (default), light

## Use it

- **VS Code:** pick *Seasonal 03 · March — St. Patrick's Day · Dark* or *Seasonal 03 · March — St. Patrick's Day · Light* with **Preferences: Color Theme**. The Seasonal Themes extension switches to it during March on its own.
- **Oh My Posh:** [davids-March.omp.json](davids-March.omp.json) (dark), [davids-March-light.omp.json](davids-March-light.omp.json) (light). `Get-SeasonalTheme.ps1` picks the right one for today.

---

Every colour role, the light-mode changes and all generated files are in [theme-definition.md](theme-definition.md). To change the month, edit [season.jsonc](season.jsonc) and run `pwsh ./Generate-Themes.ps1`.
